plugin.name: Better Web Search
plugin.description: Web search and page reading with no API key required. Works out of the box and switches backend on failure. The panel first walks you through stopping the host's built-in "web search" plugin (please do that in the Plugin Centre), then shows which route answered your last search. For more quota and steadier answers, set up an Exa key (several keys rotate) and an AnySearch key (one key) separately under Advanced. Also has proxy-compatibility switches, a network self-check and self-hosted SearXNG.
panel.title: Better Web Search
panel.subtitle: Stop the host's built-in "web search" and conversation searches come to this plugin. It works without any key.
panel.start.title: Installed — one step left
panel.start.lead: Open the host's Plugin Centre and stop its built-in "web search"; this plugin then takes over searching in conversation.
panel.start.whoClicks: This one is yours to click: the plugin no longer presses the host's switch for you.
panel.start.twoPaths: Either way works: use the shared free tier with no key, or go to Advanced and add a key for more quota and steadier answers.
panel.start.accWhere: Where to click in the Plugin Centre
panel.start.where: Host sidebar → Plugin Centre → find "Web Search" → stop it. Stopping it there also writes "start on boot" to off, so it stays down after a restart.
panel.start.reopen: This page only appears while the built-in is still running. Press the button above to check once, and it stops coming back. To see the state any time, use the card at the bottom of the Status tab.
panel.guide.freeNote: Exa registration needs no credit card. When the free money runs out it falls back to the free tier automatically — you are never charged.
panel.guide.step1.title: Step 1: register and get your key
panel.guide.step1.line1: Open this address (reachable directly, no proxy needed):
panel.guide.step1.line1b: If it will not open, copy it and paste it into your browser address bar.
panel.guide.step1.line2: Choose to sign in with e-mail. Any QQ or 163 mailbox works; if no mail arrives, check the spam folder first.
panel.guide.step1.line3: After logging in, click Create API Key, then copy the whole string. The "API Key" on that page is the key this panel means.
panel.guide.step1.qIntro: After the e-mail sign-up, Exa asks three questions. Answer them like this and you land in the console; picking differently costs you no key and no quota:
panel.guide.step1.q1: What are you coding with? — pick anything.
panel.guide.step1.q2: What integration should the prompt generate? — pick mcp.
panel.guide.step1.q3: What are you building? — pick Web search tool.
panel.guide.step1.qAfter: These three only decide which setup guide it shows you. This plugin calls the same endpoint either way, so they affect neither your quota nor your speed.
panel.guide.keyField.label: Exa key
panel.guide.keyField.help: After saving, only the last four characters are shown here. The plain key never stays in the panel or in logs; only the plugin stores it.
panel.guide.keyField.placeholderReplace: Paste a new key (saving replaces the old one)
panel.guide.urlCopied: Address copied — paste it into your browser bar.
panel.guide.copyFailed: Copy did not work. Select the address above and copy it by hand.
panel.guide.keyEmpty: Paste a key first, or leave it empty and search on the shared free tier.
panel.guide.quota: How the quota works: $20 on sign-up, then $10 refreshes every month. One search costs about $0.007, so roughly 1400 searches a month, about 47 a day. No credit card, nothing is charged when it runs out — you get a 402 and the plugin moves to the next key in the pool, then to another search source.
panel.quota.fallback: It works without a key too: the shared free tier, but slower, with lower limits, and it acts up now and then.

panel.exa.title: Exa keys (optional, several rotate)
panel.exa.accRegister: How to get an Exa key
panel.exa.step2.title: Step 2: paste it into this card's box
panel.exa.pasteLine: Tap "Add a key", click into the box and paste the whole thing with Ctrl+V. No spaces before or after.
panel.exa.step3.title: Step 3: save and use it
panel.exa.saveLine: Tap "Save and use" — the plugin runs one live search to check it. If it works, Exa becomes the preferred source; if not, it tells you why and keeps using the shared free tier, so search never breaks.
panel.key.label: Key pool
panel.keys.helpTitle: What if one key is not enough · how the quota works
panel.keys.help: Each account gets about 1400 searches a month. Register another e-mail account and add its key here: when one runs out, the plugin moves to the next.
panel.key.fallbackLabel: Try keyless once more when every key failed
panel.key.fallbackHelp: Off by default: when the whole pool failed the search goes straight to another backend and saves the time for it. On means one shared anonymous try after the full ring, which is usually gone too.
panel.any.title: AnySearch key (optional, one key)
panel.any.line: Leaving it empty still searches, and AnySearch is already the first source by default; a key only raises the limits.
panel.any.label: anysearch key
panel.any.accRegister: How to get an AnySearch key
panel.any.help: AnySearch issues free keys too; one per account, no pool and no rotation. It also decides order: with this key set, exa no longer moves up to the first slot.
panel.any.registerLine1: Open this page (reachable directly, no proxy needed), sign up or log in, and create a key in the console:
panel.any.registerLine2: Copy the whole key, paste it into the box above and tap "Save and use" — the plugin checks it with one real search.
panel.any.fieldHelp: It is stored only in this plugin's config; the panel, the logs and status reports all show any****last-4 at most.
panel.any.placeholder: Copy it from the AnySearch console
panel.note.title: A note about these two accounts
panel.note.mail: Both send marketing mail; the unsubscribe link at the bottom of any of their e-mails stops it. Your account and key keep working and your quota is untouched.
panel.trial.line1: It searches without an account on the shared free tier — slower, with lower limits. For more speed, open the tutorial below and get a key.

panel.host.title: Built-in "web search" plugin (strongly recommend stopping it)
panel.host.label: Host's built-in "web search": current state
panel.host.line: Once it is stopped, searches in conversation only ever reach this plugin.
panel.host.why: Why stop it: with two search plugins installed, the model picks which one to call each turn, so your key and your chosen chain may never get used. Stop the built-in and this plugin is the only route — your chain, your key, and you can see who answered in the "Latest search" card above.
panel.host.gate: "Sometimes she answers from memory without searching" is not decided here: the host runs its own gate first to judge whether the turn needs outside information, and when it says no, no plugin is dispatched at all. What stopping the built-in guarantees is that when she does search, it is this route.
panel.host.impact: Only two host features get dropped, and neither is load-bearing: the "window" source for proactive chat (off by default — you have to turn it on) loses its material, and proactive topic openers fall back to the plain hint instead of real titles and links. Searching in conversation, Bilibili / YouTube / Twitch trends and feeds, watch-together, and meme and music material are all unaffected.
panel.host.tradeoff: So: unless you turned on "talk to me about the window I'm looking at", stop the built-in with a clear conscience. One thing to know if you turn it back on later: the host's search gateway keeps a 5-minute failure cooldown, so for a few minutes after re-enabling, those paths may still come back empty. That is the cooldown, not a failed toggle.
panel.host.help: Read-only here; this plugin no longer flips that switch for you.
panel.host.stopHere: Still running: stop "Web Search" in the host's Plugin Centre, which also keeps it from starting on boot.
panel.host.notFound: The built-in web search was not found — it may have been removed. This plugin is unaffected.
panel.host.manualWhy: To stop it, turn "Web Search" off in the host's Plugin Centre itself: the host performs the step and also writes "start on boot" to off, so it stays stopped after a restart. This plugin no longer presses that switch for you -- that meant POSTing the host's local management API, and while the host is reloading its plugin list a press can take 8+ seconds to be answered. Until it answers, nobody can tell "it did not work" from "it worked and replied late", so changes that had landed got reported as errors. This card only reads: press "Check again" to see whether it is running.
panel.diag.title: Network check
panel.diag.help: Tries each search source one by one and tells you what works directly and how long it takes.
panel.diag.accScope: What the self-check does and does not test
panel.diag.scope: The check probes this plugin's own search channels ({chain}) — not the host's built-in search, and not the chat model.
panel.diag.exaWithKey: The exa row uses your saved key ({masked}), so it shows what a keyed request does.
panel.diag.exaAnonymous: No key saved yet: the exa row uses the shared anonymous tier, so being slow and limited is normal there.
panel.diag.hostUnrelatedOn: The host's built-in search is running, but it takes no part in this check — this plugin does not go through it.
panel.diag.hostUnrelatedOff: The host's built-in search is stopped; that changes nothing in this check.
panel.diag.cost: The check performs real searches (one per source, two with the proxy path on) and uses quota. Run it only when something feels off.
panel.diag.none: No details came back this time — it may have been too slow, or the plugin was still starting.
panel.diag.emptyResult: The check returned nothing. Try again in a moment.
panel.diag.column.name: Source
panel.diag.dual: Test through the proxy as well
panel.diag.dualAuto: Currently following the detected proxy ({state}). Switch it to decide yourself.
panel.diag.dualHelp: Doubles the probes and the quota the check costs, but it is the only way to see which sources need the proxy.
panel.net.title: Proxy compatibility
panel.net.fakeIpHelp: If your proxy hands out fake addresses (like 198.18.x.x), keep this allowed so page text can still be fetched. No idea? Leave it as it is.
